anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the USB-C receptacle J12 pin A4 (the VBUS pin) is attached to BOTH the +5V global label and the VBUS global label. On the Power sheet U5 (TPS2121RUXR) pin 1 OUT is on the VBUS net and pin 2 IN2 is on the +5V net. Because J12.A4 carries both labels, the +5V net and the VBUS net are merged into one net, so the mux's IN2 is shorted directly to its OUT, and the USB connector's VBUS pin is hard-wired to the mux output rail.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the USB VBUS pin must feed the mux input IN2 on the +5V net, and the mux output must be a separate VBUS net: 'J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2)' and 'note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.' J12.A4 should carry only the +5V label, never VBUS.

evidence.quote: J12 (USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_14P) VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2).
note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.
mcu.kicad_sch (page 1/4), top-right: J12 pin A4 wire carries a +5V global label and a VBUS global label; power.kicad_sch (page 4/4): U5 pin 1 OUT = VBUS, U5 pin 2 IN2 = +5V.

anomalies.impact: The TPS2121RUXR power mux is defeated: its IN2 and OUT are the same node, so it cannot perform seamless switchover between the 12 V barrel jack and USB. When the 12 V supply is connected, the mux output (now = VBUS = USB pin A4) drives 12 V onto the USB-C VBUS pin, back-powering the host port and potentially damaging it; the +5V/IN2 input also loses its independent source.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a net-merge anomaly: the USB-C VBUS pin (J12.A4) is labeled with both +5V and VBUS, tying the mux input IN2 to the mux output OUT and hard-wiring the USB connector to the mux output rail, which contradicts the spec's requirement that +5V (USB) and VBUS (mux output) be distinct nets and bypasses the power-mux arbitration.
